messages:
maria: FYI, ZenLake renewal coming up. They want to rebaseline pricing after the POC — asking for a reduction in the annual commit and a credit for overage during the POC. Can deal-desk weigh in?

nina: @maria can you drop the current numbers and the contract term? need the rate-card line items and whether there's any existing concession in the quote.

maria: Current committed ARR: $120,000/yr. Term runs through 12/2026. POC consumed ~120k tokens and incurred ~$9k overage this quarter. Customer asking to reduce commit to ~$85k for next year and wants a one-time credit for the $9k.

josh: CS notes: ZenLake was happy with throughput and routing, we saw usage spike during POC but it's expected to normalize. They're a good expansion candidate (security ok but want SSO + audit logs).

raj: On the POC side: we covered a staging node discount (50% off infra for POC) but they spun up extra test jobs. We can show a breakdown: infra credits + token overage.

nina: Baseline rules: deal-desk only approves adjustments if compensated by term length, case for future expansion, or documented exec signoff. We usually do either (a) one-time credit and keep commit, (b) pro-rate commit change midterm with an amendment + revenue protection clause, or (c) apply a true-up with an upsell commitment.

adrian: Legal: any amendment needs to include effective date and a clause that prevents retroactive resets of committed volumes. If you offer a credit, we should document scope (POC only) and exclude it from future credits.

maria: Looking for recommended approach. Customer argues the POC was larger than expected and wants the commit lowered now to avoid churn. They will sign a 24-month renewal if we do a partial rebaseline + modest credit.

nina: Ask for a short justification email from customer (1-2 lines) agreeing to 24-month term in exchange for the concession. Then we can propose these options to sales leadership: 
- Option 1: One-time credit = $9,000, keep $120k commit, 24-month renewal.
- Option 2: Rebaseline to $90k/yr for 24 months + one-time credit $4,000 (split the delta).
- Option 3: Accept $85k/yr for 12 months, then revert to standard rate-card; require signed amendment + PO.

raj: If we go with Option 2 we should require a 30% usage cap for first 3 months and the right to revert if usage exceeds threshold — preserves economics.

josh: CS is fine with Option 2 if customer agrees to 24-months. That gives retention + predictable spending.

nina: Financials quick calc (approx):
```
Current ARR: $120,000
Option2 ARR: 90,000 -> annual delta = -30,000
Assume 24 months -> total delta = -60,000 vs original expectation
One-time credit we propose: 4,000 (absorbed by sales reserves)
Net impact over 2 years ~ -64k (but prevents churn and enables expansion)
```

adrian: Also need procurement/legal to confirm PO flow for 24-months. If they want early termination rights we should decline or charge early termination fees.

maria: We have a verbal from their VP product for 24 months. I'll get the email confirmation today. @nina what approvals do you need for Option 2?

nina: Submit a Deal Desk request with: customer justification email, commercial summary (new ARR/term), any CS enablement notes, and the recommended revenue concession. I need VP-Sales or Head of Growth approval for anything > $50k net concession.

sec-bot: SECURITY: ZenLake still has outstanding SQ items: SOC2 evidence and SSO scoping. Closing those reduces friction for renewal. Link to tracker: https://redwood-internal/zenlake/sec-track

maria: Noted — I'll attach the SQ responses and SSH logs.

josh: I'll prep a short deployment SOW and runbook for the renewal bundle.

nina: If you can get the email and the SQ evidence by EOD, I can fast-track to VP approvals tomorrow.

maria: Will do. Thanks all. I'll post the customer email here when I have it. :thumbsup:
